Watch a Kubernetes list endpoint

Source: R/watch.R
Watch.Rd

Watch a Kubernetes list endpoint

Watch a Kubernetes list endpoint

Details

Streams watch events (ADDED/MODIFIED/DELETED/BOOKMARK/ERROR) from any list endpoint that supports ?watch=true. Mirrors the Python client's kubernetes.watch.Watch and client-go's watch.Interface.

The server returns line-delimited JSON; each line is a WatchEvent with type and object fields. The object's resourceVersion is tracked so the stream can be resumed after a 410 Gone.

There are two ways to consume a watch:

  • $stream() blocks and calls a callback for each event.

  • $open(), then $poll() repeatedly, then $close(). poll() returns the events that have arrived (waiting at most max_wait seconds), so a single R process can drive several watches from one loop. When the server ends a connection normally, poll() reconnects from the last resourceVersion, so callers see one continuous stream.

Public fields

resource_version

Last observed resourceVersion. Used to resume.

stop_requested

Set to TRUE by $stop() to break the loop.

end_reason

Why the watch ended: "stop" (the callback returned FALSE, or $stop() / $close() was called), "timeout" (timeout_seconds elapsed), or "gone" (410 Gone with return_on_gone = TRUE). NULL while the watch is open.

Method stream()

Stream events to a callback.

Usage

Watch$stream(
  client,
  resource_path,
  query_params = list(),
  callback,
  timeout_seconds = NULL,
  resource_version = NULL,
  return_on_gone = FALSE
)

Arguments

client

An ApiClient.

resource_path

Path template for the list endpoint, with path parameters already substituted (e.g. "/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods").

query_params

Additional query parameters (label selectors etc.). watch=true is added automatically.

callback

Function function(type, object) invoked for each event. Return FALSE to stop the stream.

timeout_seconds

Total wall-clock budget for the whole call. The stream reconnects after normal server hang-ups while time remains and returns once it is spent, even if no events arrive. NULL (default) watches until the callback returns FALSE or $stop() is called.

resource_version

Starting resourceVersion (defaults to last seen).

return_on_gone

If TRUE, return with end_reason = "gone" on 410 Gone so the caller can re-list (this is what Informer does). If FALSE (default), restart the watch without a resourceVersion, which replays the current state as ADDED events but cannot report objects deleted while the watch was disconnected.

Method open()

Open the watch for polling with $poll().

Usage

Watch$open(
  client,
  resource_path,
  query_params = list(),
  resource_version = NULL,
  timeout_seconds = NULL,
  server_timeout = NULL,
  return_on_gone = FALSE
)

Arguments

client, resource_path, query_params, resource_version, return_on_gone

As for $stream().

timeout_seconds

Optional overall limit; once it passes, poll() closes the watch with end_reason = "timeout".

server_timeout

Optional timeoutSeconds for each connection. The server ends the connection after this long and poll() reconnects. NULL leaves it to the server (usually 30-60 minutes).

Method poll()

Return the events that have arrived, waiting up to max_wait seconds for the first one.

Usage

Watch$poll(max_wait = 0)

Arguments

max_wait

Seconds to wait when nothing is pending (default 0: just collect what is already there).

Returns

A list of events, each list(type, object, resource_version). Empty when nothing arrived or the watch is closed.

Close a watch opened with $open().

Usage

Watch$close()

Method stop()

Ask the watch to end: $stream() returns after the current event, and the next $poll() closes the watch.

Usage

Watch$stop()

Method clone()

The objects of this class are cloneable with this method.

Usage

Watch$clone(deep = FALSE)

Arguments

deep

Whether to make a deep clone.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
client <- new_client_from_config()
w <- Watch$new()
w$stream(
  client,
  resource_path = "/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods",
  callback = function(type, object) {
    cat(type, object$metadata$name, "\n")
    TRUE  # keep watching
  },
  timeout_seconds = 30
)

# Polling
w <- Watch$new()
w$open(client, "/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods")
repeat {
  for (e in w$poll(1)) cat(e$type, e$object$metadata$name, "\n")
}
} # }
